<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the

- These devices sometimes do not respond on the first try
  or may be subject to transient broadcast failures, or
  overloads. We now try discovery periodically once the
  integration has been loaded.

<sub><sup>(message by IssueLinks)</sup></sub>
Old Issue for reference that had similar problem: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/45943

Now each device is listed separately in the integration UI. I have 52 devices and I get a tiny window with long list and scroll bar that is hard to scroll (looks great on mobile though). It is possible to list all entities/devices like before (and like other integrations where they have two links one for devices and other for entities).

Is it now working though? If not, you should enable the debug logging for `homeassistant.components.tplink` to see if you receive any useful errors from the integration itself. If that doesn't bring any ideas why it might be failing,  you can also enable `kasa` for debug logging, but bear in mind that this will produce looooooots of output especially with so many devices, as it will print every outgoing and incoming response.

To your earlier problems, as you mention that it got fixed earlier by resetting your router, this problem might be in your router (some routers are known not to perform well if they have lots of devices connected to them) and not in the integration itself... Could that be possible in this case?

On the UI issue – I don't like the UI myself either when there are lots of devices, but improving the UI is out of the scope of any issues you are having with the tplink integration. I think https://github.com/home-assistant/frontend/discussions is the correct location for submitting enhancement proposals.

edit: Oh, I forgot to mention that after the devices have been configured (or imported from yaml, as should be the case in your case) you can always go to the "Devices" tab (Configuration -> Devices) which will list all devices you have. If you search "tp-link" you will get a list of all the devices and you can access the entities by clicking the device entry which is a bit more comfortable than the small list on the integrations tab :-)

Thank you for the suggestions.

I understand that my router is in question, but all devices continue working fine otherwise including TP-Link via their app. It is just that HA does not see those devices. I'm not sure why this happens only after applying the update. (I use a Unifi Dream Machine Pro with 4 Nano HD access points in my home. These are considered enterprise grade.)

I'm also holding back from resetting my router this time and be able to find the root cause of this lingering issue.

I will enable logging for tplink and see what shows up. Will report back soon.
